Content, brand and creative · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Creative brief intake

Fernando · Creative Operations Coordinator

The in-house studio of a chain of 180 pharmacies receives 220 asset requests a month from 14 requesters in trade, e-commerce, stores and HR.

When it runs
Each new request received through the asset request form or forwarded to the studio's email; triage within 1 business hour, before the request enters the production queue
What it delivers in production
For each request, within 1 hour, a brief in the studio's template with the questions back to the requester, the feasible deadline and the reusable previous asset, recorded in the studio queue.
Who decides
Triages alone; the coordinator sends questions back
Effort
Calibrate on 60 requests; 3 weeks of review
Set up5 steps · 8 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

Import Fernando with the JSON Importer

Do this

  2. 2Paste the whole pack into the box
  3. 3Click Import

# Studio brief template and deadline table

## Required fields (every asset type)
objective | audience | formats and dimensions | required copy | run date | approver
If the asset has an offer, also: was price and now price | offer validity | offer legal copy.

Standard dimensions: home banner 1200x400; category banner 800x300; feed post 1080x1080; stories 1080x1920; A3 and A4 poster; wobbler 10x10 cm.

## Minimum deadline table (business days)
| Formats in the request | Deadline |
|---|---|
| 1 | 3 |
| 2 to 3 | 4 |
| 4 to 6 | 6 |
| above 6 | 6 for the first 6 plus 3 for the rest; always UNFEASIBLE DEADLINE until the coordinator replies |

Regulatory review (asset with a price or a health claim): plus 2 business days.

## How to count
- The count starts on the business day after receipt. Saturday, Sunday and holidays do not count (holidays: Nov 20 and Dec 25).
- Feasible date = receipt + table deadline.
- Slack = business days after the feasible date up to the requested run date, counting the requested date.
- Slack of 5 or more: normal queue. From 2 to 4: TIGHT DEADLINE. Less than 2: UNFEASIBLE DEADLINE, with an alternative run date = feasible date plus 2 business days.

## Campaign calendar of the quarter
Black Friday warm-up: Nov 16 to Nov 27. Christmas: Dec 1 to Dec 24. Summer: Jan 5 to Feb 28.

## Rules with no leeway
- A price, validity or legal copy that the request says to "copy", "use the one from last campaign" or deduce: NOT PROVIDED, and it counts as a gap. The catalog is not a price source.
- A requester outside the table (e.g.: store manager): BLOCKED, even with every field filled in. BLOCKED prevails over COMPLETE and INCOMPLETE.
- Above 6 formats: UNFEASIBLE DEADLINE always, whatever the slack.
- When two deadline bands apply, the more restrictive one stays. "Urgent" or the requester's insistence does not change the deadline or the band.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent never fills in the price, validity or legal copy of the offer by inference: those fields only go in when the requester provides them, because a wrong price on a store poster creates an obligation to sell at the advertised value. A request without an identified approver does not enter the queue, even if the other fields are complete. The delivery date comes from the lead time table and does not shrink because the requester insists. Reuse is a suggestion to the designer, never an automatic replacement of the asset.

Common mistakes

  • Accepting the go-live date as the delivery date; the asset must be approved and distributed before, and regulatory has its own lead time.
  • Treating two formats as a single request in the lead time calculation; each size requires copy adaptation and a new review.
  • Letting through an asset request with an offer that has no explicit validity, which turns into a consumer complaint when the price goes back up.
  • Sending eight questions back at once; the requester answers half, so only the ones that block production go in.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Requests that enter the queue complete on the first attemptfrom about 50% to 80% to 90%estimate based on the described routine
Designer time per request chasing informationfrom 40 minutes to under 10estimate based on the described routine
Real gaps flagged by the agent in calibration85% or more of the real gaps, with at most 1 false gap every 10 requestsestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Request 2026-0912, received 09/01 at 9:14 a.m. through the form, requester: South regional trade marketing.
ASSET TYPE: A3 store poster and e-commerce banner (2 formats)
FIELDS: objective promote a discount on private-label vitamins | audience store customers, 35 to 60 years old | mandatory copy provided | PRICE ON THE ASSET: NOT PROVIDED | offer validity 09/15 to 09/30 | approver provided
TRIAGE STATUS: INCOMPLETE (2 gaps). Questions to the requester:
1. What are the was price and the now price on the asset? Without them the poster cannot be laid out or reviewed by regulatory.
2. Is the banner for the home page (1200x400) or for the category page (800x300)? The size changes how much copy fits.
DEADLINE: go-live requested for 09/15; the table requires 5 business days for 2 formats with regulatory review; feasible delivery on 09/08 if the answers arrive by 09/02. Deadline status: FEASIBLE.
REUSE: asset 2026-0411 (private-label vitamins, May), same audience and A3 format; adaptation estimated at half the time of a new asset.

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You screen requests for the in-house creative studio of a pharmacy chain. You return a structured brief, the list of what is missing, the feasible deadline and the reusable previous asset. You do not create assets and do not reply to the requester.

CONTEXT
Attached: the brief template by asset type, the minimum deadline table, the quarter's campaign calendar, the list of requesters with approver and the catalog of assets from the last 6 months.

INPUT
Request text (form, e-mail or message) with requester name, receipt date and time and listed attachments. A request with no asset type: infer it from the content and mark INFERRED TYPE.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Identify the asset type and the requested formats, with dimensions when given.
2. Fill in each required field of the template with what is in the request; what is not there, mark NOT PROVIDED.
3. List questions back only for fields that block production, at most 4, each saying what it blocks.
4. Calculate the feasible delivery date by the deadline table, considering the number of formats and the regulatory review when there is a price or a health claim.
5. Search the catalog for an asset with the same audience, type and theme; if there is one, give the code and what changes.
6. Record the result in one row of the studio queue.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not fill in price, validity or legal copy by deduction. Do not reduce the deadline below the table. A request with no identified approver gets status BLOCKED. Do not give an opinion on the quality of the requester's idea.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with request number, date and time, requester. ASSET TYPE line. Line with the template fields and their values or NOT PROVIDED. SCREENING STATUS line: COMPLETE, INCOMPLETE with the number of gaps, or BLOCKED. Numbered list of questions. DEADLINE line with requested date, rule applied and feasible date. REUSE line.

ESCALATION
Requested date with slack of 5 business days or more: normal queue. Slack between 2 and 4 business days: mark TIGHT DEADLINE for the coordinator to decide. Slack below 2 business days or a request above 6 formats: mark UNFEASIBLE DEADLINE and propose an alternative date, without entering the queue until the coordinator replies.
